engine.build: pypi sglang==0.5.20 (py3.12 venv, torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer-python 0.6.18, sglang-kernel 0.4.7)

conditions.detail: Only this SGLang server (and, for the speed and long-context rows, the small cache-busting proxy in front of it) was resident; the image server that normally runs on the box was stopped, and nvidia-smi listed no other compute process. The only other running container was a small host metrics exporter (python, about 10 MB, no GPU).
conditions.isolation_check: nvidia-smi compute apps -> 1532664, .venv/bin/python 1532720, sglang::scheduler ; docker ps -> 1 containers; load1 at start 0.92

gotchas.text: Tool calling needs SGLang with the minicpm5 tool-call parser (sgl-project/sglang#25600). The openbmb cookbook says to install SGLang from main because v0.5.12.post1 lacked it; the PyPI 0.5.20 wheel used here ships it, so no source build is needed any more. The model writes XML tool calls (<function name="x"><param name="k">v</param></function>) and they come back as OpenAI tool_calls with finish_reason tool_calls, with thinking on and off.

SGLang has no MiniCPM5 reasoning parser, but the model uses plain <think> ... </think>, so --reasoning-parser qwen3 splits it into reasoning_content. With enable_thinking left unset the template adds no <think> prefix; the model opens the tag itself and the qwen3 parser still catches it.

flashinfer JIT-compiles its prefill kernels on the first request and shells out to ninja. In a venv that is not activated the first prefill dies with FileNotFoundError: ninja and the scheduler exits; put the venv bin directory on PATH before starting the server.
In a llama.cpp deployment the card warns that the default min_p 0.05 causes repetition and asks for min_p 0; the SGLang default min_p is already 0.

SGLang RadixAttention reuses any cached prefix and has no per-request switch to skip it, and the prefill, long-context and serving workloads reuse the same prompts and haystacks. To keep prefill cold without turning the cache off for the whole server, the speed and long-context rows went through a small proxy on the box that prepends a unique HTML comment (<!-- 12 hex chars -->, about 12 tokens) to the first message of every request, so the shared prefix is only the few chat-template tokens before it. Input token counts include the comment.

DSpark does not start on this box with SGLang 0.5.20 at the default decode CUDA-graph size. DSpark verifies block_size+1 = 8 tokens per sequence, so capturing the decode graph at its default max batch of 256 asks flashinfer for a 3,137,536-byte prefill workspace out of a fixed 1,048,576-byte AlignedAllocator and capture fails with a buffer overflow, taking the scheduler with it. 0.5.20 exposes no workspace-size flag, so the only knob is --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode; it is set to 64 here and recorded in the args. That leaves admission alone - max_running_requests is still 512 and still confirmed from /get_server_info - but batches above 64 run without a captured decode graph, so the concurrency points above 64 in this config are NOT arg-identical to the plain bf16 2B rows and the two should not be diffed at those points. The single-user and low-concurrency rows are the comparable ones.

The DSpark drafter costs KV pool: max_total_num_tokens falls from 2,034,852 on the plain 2B to 1,798,013 here at the same --mem-fraction-static 0.75, and the drafter itself loads as a separate 0.93 GB Qwen3DSparkModel.

The 128 and 256 points of this sweep first measured a flat 100 concurrent requests: atlas-bench built its httpx.AsyncClient without a limits argument, and httpx defaults to max_connections=100, so requests 101 and up waited in the client connection pool. SGLang itself was idle enough to take them (max_running_requests 512 from /get_server_info, #queue-req 0 in the scheduler log the whole time), so the plateau looked like an engine knee and was not one. The first attempt was discarded; the numbers here come from a rerun with the pool sized to the sweep's own top level (inference-atlas PR #233), and the scheduler log shows #running-req reaching 256 with #queue-req 0. Any engine measured above 100 concurrent requests with an unpatched atlas-bench has the same problem.

provenance.notes: Weights: openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B at 12a3808a956f869c767195e9266b59c4d21d92e2, BF16, sha256 checked against the Hub. Speculative decoding with the card-recommended DSpark drafter openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B-DSpark at 114a20fdbf53220712c7fbdd7dccddbf1dedebb4 (BF16, 5 layers, 324M parameters, 0.65 GB), --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 7 as in the model card. SGLang 0.5.20 from PyPI in a Python 3.12 venv (uv) with torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer-python 0.6.18, sglang-kernel 0.4.7, triton 3.7.1, transformers 5.12.1, xgrammar 0.2.1; CUDA 13.0, driver 580.173.02, Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel 6.17.0-1029-nvidia. Environment SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1 and SGLANG_DISABLE_CUDNN_CHECK=1 as the MiniCPM SGLang cookbook recommends, the venv bin directory on PATH (flashinfer JIT needs ninja). Server flags follow the openbmb SGLang cookbook (docs/deployment/sglang.md): --dtype bfloat16 --context-length 131072 --tool-call-parser minicpm5, plus --reasoning-parser qwen3 so the <think> block lands in reasoning_content; --mem-fraction-static 0.75 instead of the cookbook 0.85 to leave the unified-memory box about 20 GB of host headroom (the KV pool still holds about 2 million tokens). Radix prefix cache, chunked prefill 8192, CUDA graphs and the flashinfer attention backend are SGLang defaults. Every request sets temperature 0 and seed 42 as the workloads specify. The chat template has three thinking states: enable_thinking true prefills <think>, false prefills an empty think block, and unset lets the model decide, which on almost every prompt means it thinks. Speed and long-context depth rows send chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking false; eval and needle rows leave it unset (the template default). Load: target weights 36.8 s (5.01 GB) plus the DSpark drafter 3.5 s (0.93 GB, loaded as Qwen3DSparkModel), KV allocation 3.6 s, CUDA graphs prefill 17.4 s / target-verify 2.5 s / draft-decode 1.7 s, scheduler end to end 71.2 s; SGLang reported max_total_num_tokens 1,798,013 (down from the plain 2B's 2,034,852 because the drafter and the verify buffers take their share) and 22.7 GB of GPU memory still free. max_running_requests is passed explicitly as 512 and confirmed at 512 from /get_server_info before the first concurrent row. Harness provenance: this row was measured with bench/atlas_bench/client.py and bench/atlas_bench/runner.py taken from inference-atlas PR #233 (branch bench/httpx-connection-pool-limit, commit a8d5c694ffba6ebe917152bf7ba9519097a857bd), applied on top of main at f21d09f. That change sizes the httpx connection pool from the widest concurrency in the packet instead of leaving httpx at its default max_connections=100. An unpatched checkout caps this workload at 100 concurrent requests, which makes its 128 and 256 points meaningless; the points at 64 and below are identical either way, because the pool is never the limit there. To reproduce this row exactly, check out main at f21d09f and apply that PR.
